findings.body:
Removal of `escapeHtml` combined with passing raw `body` to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` allows arbitrary HTML (including script tags) from the `body` prop to execute in the browser.

If `body` contains user-controlled content (comments), an attacker can inject `<script>`, event handlers, or other payloads that run with the viewer's origin.

```suggestion
  return <div className="comment" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: escapeHtml(body) }} />;
```

(Verified: `escapeHtml` existed on lines 3-5 of the base file; no sanitization or callers that pre-escape were found in the diff scope.)

summary: Critical XSS vulnerability introduced by removing HTML escaping and passing unsanitized `body` directly to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and passes the raw body prop into dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so attacker-controlled comment HTML can execute in the viewer’s origin. Base still escaped </>/&; head has no replacement sanitizer.
